notes: WebSearch could not be used for this part (the session's search budget, 200 searches, was already spent), so pages were reached directly: the campaign websites filed with the Secretary of State (read from John's saved lists by the kit's own reader, python -m ballot.local_sites files, on a scratch copy of the database), government, party and newspaper sites, and the search pages of two newspapers (hometownsource.com, winonapost.com). Candidates with nothing below are ones for whom no such page stated anything a card may show.

Sites that asked scripts to stay out or refused them: co.ym.mn.gov and co.wabasha.mn.us (robots.txt). Those two counties' commissioner pages were opened before their robots.txt was checked; nothing read there is used, so Greg Renneke and Rick Powers have no findings here. A person can read the two pages by hand: https://www.co.ym.mn.gov/commissioners and https://www.co.wabasha.mn.us/government/board_of_commissioners/index.php. columbiaheightsmn.gov and sartellmn.com (robots.txt; opened before the check, nothing used). mncourts.gov (403 on its judicial directory and on its robots.txt: no court page for Judges Staples and Rosenfeldt). mn.gov/governor (a CAPTCHA page; left at once). ballotpedia.org (an empty page to scripts). dfl-cd2.org (403).

Tim Miller (East Bethel, Council Member At Large): the City of East Bethel's own notice says the council member of that name, who had filed for re-election, died on August 1, 2026, and that his name stays on the November 3 ballot. It is recorded as a review item for John to read; how the page should show it is his decision.

Read and left out on purpose: jobs and employers, schools, family, religion, nonprofit boards and military service (the Legislative Reference Library's records and the campaign sites show some of these); labor and other non-party endorsements; a legislative staff post and a county attorney's office post in Karla Bigham's record, and a second 2025 appointment there whose wording is unclear. Charlotte Gabler's filed address (votegabler.com) shows only "Launching Soon" and names nobody, so no website finding is made for her.

Birth years: the Legislative Reference Library gives Robert Farnsworth's date of birth as June 17, 1978 and marks it "(uncertain)"; the Minnesota Historical Election Archive gives the same date without that mark. The year is recorded from the archive, as secondary, with the library's mark said in the source line.

party_support (a key the loader does not read, in the shape other parts use): two party units list candidates of this part on pages that do not use the word endorsed: the 8th Congressional District Republicans' "2026 Candidates" (Farnsworth, Warwas) and the Winona County Republicans' "Candidates" (Repinski). They are kept apart from endorsed_by so that no page calls them endorsements; whether and how they are shown is John's decision. The St. Louis County Republican Party's list is under endorsed_by because its home page calls it "the candidates endorsed by the St. Louis County Republican Party for 2026 elections".

Two filed campaign sites still carry the text of an earlier run: repinskiforhouse.com (his first run; no 2026 date) and klangforsheriff.com (his 2022 announcement, under a 2026 copyright line). Both are the addresses filed for 2026.

Steve Soyka: Stearns County's own pages show their text only through scripts, so no official page is given. The county's news item of January 8, 2019 ("Steve Soyka was sworn-in as the new Sheriff") is in the news data that its Sheriff's Office page loads and can be seen in the page source; a reader in a browser may not see it. Alyssa Bowers: the Waseca district's directory address carries her family name as its search word, since the directory shows her only when searched.

verifier_notes: Every address in the file was opened again on 2026-10-02 with the kit's own User-Agent; all 40 answered. Each finding was read against the page and against the race in our record (state plus office, place or district).
The St. Louis County Republican Party's list is no longer under endorsed_by (see removed): this replaces the last sentence of the researcher's sixth note.

Two findings are stated only in a page's source data, not in its visible text without scripts: Steve Soyka's swearing-in (Stearns County news item dated 2019-01-08) and Sarah Grovender's "First Elected/Appointed: January 2017" (North Branch Area Public Schools). Both were found there as recorded.

The reference to WJON's March 2, 2023 profile of Steve Soyka was taken out of the source line: that page is not among the addresses and was not opened. The sentence about Karla Bigham's About page was taken out for the same reason.
Official pages for Koch, Contreras, Gabler, Grovender, Polcher, Bigham and Schiefelbein also show phone numbers, e-mail or an address; none of that is in this file.
